newsitem.title: FINLAND: Idle Helsinki plods to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Idle Helsinki plods to lower close.

text.p: Shares ended a mixed session lower on Monday, with trade stagnant as many players were on holiday or on hold ahead of key U.S. data this week and Nokia's first-half report due next Monday, brokers said.
The FOX index fell 0.36 percent to 1,217.69, and the all-share HEX ended off 0.38 percent at 3,529.86 points. Volume was a paltry 325 million markka, after big volumes last week.
But with the Dow industrials starting higher, bulls refused to be penned. "I don't see any fundamental reason this market should turn, even if these levels are insane," one broker said.

Brokers said Helsinki -- along with other bourses -- would be a captive audience to key U.S. indicators this week, including Q2 employment cost data on Tuesday, Q2 GDP on Thursday and July non-farm payrolls on Friday.
"I don't think any of these figures can turn this market entirely," one said. "The money won't just vanish."

Nokia A closed off 1.70 markka at 44.20 after hovering in positive ground for most of the session. Nokia's less traded K share dragged the index, ending off 6.00 at 449.00. But trade in both shares was a thin 100 million markka.
Brokers said Nokia may well stay quiet before its H1 report.
As Nokia's H1 approaches after an upbeat surprise from Ericsson, analysts continued to upgrade forecasts. An options source said trade was scant, but seemed mainly bullish.

Merita led financials lower, ending down 0.40 markka at 23.80, pruning recent sharp gains. Amer closed up 3.30 at 91.30 after lively trade ahead of a decision expected from this week on whether to redeem vote-heavy K shares sold at end-June to British investor Lord Moyne, brokers said.
Small cap Incap rose 5.10 markka to 65.00 on expectations of sales growth for the company which subcontracts to both Nokia and Ericsson, brokers said.
